clue.text: One way to expand MP's permit

parts.note: the two letters M and P are each written out in full: M as its spoken name EM, P as the word it abbreviates in physics, POWER

explanation.surface: A suggestion for how a Member of Parliament might enlarge their official licence.
explanation.walkthrough: MP looks like a Member of Parliament, but here it is just two letters to spell out: the letter M is pronounced 'em', and P is the standard abbreviation for power.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone authority or the right to act is to allow them, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Biblical book, unknown in time

indicators.note: puts the unknown inside the period

parts.note: an era is a period of time
z is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A book of the Bible, of uncertain date.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Old Testament account of the return of the Jews from exile in Babylon.

clue.text: Tart in live performance initially reversing vehicle

indicators.note: the whole assembled string is read backwards
puts the sour word inside the existing one

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
acid is sour or sharp, as tart can be

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tart appears in a live show at the start of a vehicle going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives BACIDE, 'initially' adds P, and 'reversing' turns BACIDEP round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal-powered rickshaw carrying passengers is a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Grass with post-crime police activity

parts.note: heat is slang for intense police pressure after a crime

explanation.surface: An informer gets caught up in the police crackdown after a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The cereal crop is botanically a member of the grass family.

clue.text: Keep interrupting row about updated component

indicators.note: the whole combination is turned round
the stronghold breaks into the middle of the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
a keep is a castle stronghold, a fort

explanation.surface: A castle disrupting an argument about a new part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' gives TIFORTER and 'about' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A part added to existing equipment to modernise it is the noun sense of this word.

clue.text: Capital college

definitions.meaning: the chief city of Newfoundland and Labrador in Canada, and also of Antigua and Barbuda
a college of that name exists at both Oxford and Cambridge universities

explanation.surface: Two words that could describe a splendid university, or a seat of learning in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The same saint's name serves both a Canadian provincial seat of government and colleges at Oxford and Cambridge.

clue.text: Steadfast astronaut losing limb

indicators.note: the limb is dropped from the astronaut's name

parts.note: Neil Armstrong was the first man on the Moon
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A determined space traveller loses an arm or leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and resolute, a steadfast person is unwavering and robust in their resolve.

clue.text: Heroine of German agreement accommodating nothing Franco ordered

indicators.note: the German word for yes takes in the zero

parts.note: ja is German for yes
o looks like zero

indicators.note: says the letters of the dictator's name are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A wartime heroine's role in a German treaty with the Spanish dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' turns FRANCO into NOFARC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maid of Orleans led French forces in the Hundred Years' War and is a national heroine.

clue.text: Expecting to double power for making transatlantic flight?

indicators.note: the single P of the word is replaced by two

parts.note: hoping is expecting

explanation.surface: Planning to increase engine power to fly across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: Hopping across 'the pond' is jocular for crossing the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: A short trip by air is a hop, so flying the Atlantic is playfully called a hop across.

clue.text: Categorise abstract poetry in abridged guide

indicators.note: puts the rearranged poetry inside the shortened guide
the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to steer is to guide

indicators.note: says the letters of poetry are rearranged

explanation.surface: Classifying modern abstract verse in a condensed handbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abstract' turns POETRY into REOTYP, which goes in STEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pigeonhole someone with a fixed, oversimplified label is to classify them by type.

clue.text: Memorable dog having left for second

indicators.note: L for left takes the place of S for second, so one letter of the dog is swapped

parts.note: a red setter is an Irish breed of gundog

explanation.surface: A dog worth remembering because it once came first after leaving another behind.
explanation.walkthrough: L (left) replaces S (second) in RED SETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Saints' days and festivals were printed in red on calendars, so a special, memorable day came to be called this.

clue.text: Fruit tree separated from fruit

indicators.note: says the tree is pulled away from the fruit named, leaving the remainder

parts.note: a tropical fruit with a spiky crown
a pine is a coniferous tree

explanation.surface: A tree parted from its crop, as in an orchard harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'fruit' is PINEAPPLE; take away PINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A common orchard crop is an example of the general category of edible produce from a plant.

clue.text: Openly belittle OCD advice to quilt maker?

definitions.meaning: to humble someone publicly, deflating their self-importance
a fussy obsessive might tell a quilt maker to trim the feather filling to exactly the right dimensions

explanation.surface: Mocking someone in public, then advising an obsessive crafter.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'down' as the soft feathers used to fill a quilt or eiderdown.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reduce someone's inflated opinion of themselves, often in front of others.

clue.text: What could spawn new desires, for example

definitions.text: What could spawn new desires, for example

indicators.note: suggests the letters could be bred into something different

explanation.surface: Asking what breeds fresh wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could spawn' rearranges N + DESIRES + EG, and the whole clue describes the answer: avarice breeds yet more wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an insatiable vice that keeps creating more wants for wealth and possessions.

clue.text: Overturning beer ban, is a French writer

indicators.note: turning over the two words puts their combined letters back to front

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A French author campaigns to lift a prohibition on beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overturning' reverses ALE + BAR to give RABELA; IS is added.
explanation.definitionFit: François Rabelais was the sixteenth-century French author of Gargantua and Pantagruel, famous for bawdy humour.

clue.text: Large well-known store ruined immediately

parts.note: the Swedish furniture retailer
shot means worn out or ruined

explanation.surface: A big famous shop has been wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means without hesitation, as fast as a bullet.

clue.text: Trapped in yard, you say?

indicators.note: signals a word that is pronounced like another in standard British speech

parts.note: a court is an enclosed yard

explanation.surface: Someone confined in a yard, seeking confirmation.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, 'court' and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Being trapped and being captured both describe something seized and unable to escape.

clue.text: Pitch isn't black when it's this

definitions.text: Pitch isn't black when it's this

parts.words: Pitch isn't black when it's this
parts.note: pitch suggests black tar, but here it is a sports field lit up by powerful lamps

explanation.surface: A paradox about tar not being dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch-black' is the expected phrase; the pitch is a playing field illuminated for a night match.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports ground illuminated by tall banks of lamps for evening games is not dark.

clue.text: Mistake rued, partly retracted in bingo?

indicators.note: retracted says the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone regrets an error and withdraws it, perhaps in a game of bingo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' takes AKERUE from 'Mistake rued' and 'retracted' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of triumph at a discovery or success, the Greek cry attributed to Archimedes.

clue.text: Minister yet again to hold back

parts.note: re is a prefix meaning again
to minister to is to serve

explanation.surface: A cleric or politician holding back once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something aside for later use is to retain it rather than release it.

clue.text: Conservative puts away records

parts.note: to lock up is to imprison or put away

explanation.surface: A Tory politician jails people.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate or register a total, such as miles on a car or wins in a season, is to record them.

clue.text: Local name for land I found in small strip

indicators.note: the I sits inside the strip

parts.note: a verge is a grass strip beside a road

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a country's own name on a small strip of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Sverige is what the Swedes themselves call Sweden, the land's native name.

clue.text: Balanced stock book getting put away

indicators.note: the abbreviation is stowed inside the other word

parts.note: stale goods are old stock kept too long

explanation.surface: A ledger of stocks is balanced and filed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something steady and in equilibrium is not likely to fall or change.

clue.text: Drink no longer available in canteens — it changed

indicators.note: puts the word for unavailable inside the rearranged letters
says the letters of the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: a dish that is off is no longer on the menu

explanation.surface: Some beverage has disappeared from works cafeterias since it was altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns CANTEENS IT into INSTANTCEE; 'in' places OFF inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick beverage made from soluble granules is one kind of thing you drink.

clue.text: Commentator's wrongly felt for all the runners

indicators.note: a commentator speaks, so signals the spoken version

parts.note: feeled is a mistaken past form of feel

explanation.surface: A sports commentator gets a verb wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The ungrammatical past tense 'feeled' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In a race, the entire set of competitors is collectively the field.

clue.text: Massive stop after start is annulled

indicators.note: the opening letter is cancelled

parts.note: avast is the sailor's command to stop

explanation.surface: A huge halt after something begun is cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous and immense, both describe something of very great size.

clue.text: Move first to last in middle ground

indicators.note: tells the solver to take the opening letter and put it at the end

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre

explanation.surface: An instruction for a race or game: shift from front to back while in the centre of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move first to last' sends the H of HEART to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil or land underfoot is the substance we stand on, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Edited liberal article about Fonteyn, perhaps

indicators.note: says the letters of the following word are reworked into a new order
the article is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A revised progressive article written about a famous dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edited' turns LIBERAL into BALLERI; 'about' turns AN into NA. Margot Fonteyn was a celebrated British dancer with the Royal Ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Margot Fonteyn is an example of a female classical dancer.

clue.text: Pet survey cut short by obligation

indicators.note: the final letter is lopped off the word

parts.note: to sweep is to look over a whole area
a tie is something that binds you, a duty

explanation.surface: An inspection of an animal was ended early because of a prior commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the last letter from SWEEP, leaving SWEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment for a loved one, like darling, is what pet means here.

clue.text: The largest bird withers inwardly

indicators.note: the drooping word goes inside the bird

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
to wither is to die off

explanation.surface: The biggest bird is shrivelling within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tidy' can mean considerable, as in 'a tidy sum', so the superlative means largest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidy sum is a substantial one, so the most such amount is the greatest.
